items.title_orig: Reece Gonzales of Identity Crisis Talks New EP, Grunge Revival & More
items.article_text:
Jason and Paul welcome Identity Crisis lead singer Reece Gonzales to the show other discuss his young band's new EP, keeping the spirit of grunge and alt-rock alive in 2026, songwriting, and much, much more. Reece talks about the challenges of trying to make it in an AI and social media driven world and who influenced his love for our favorite bands. Identity Crisis' new EP Starve is out now -- streaming everywhere and available on vinyl on their website.

items.title_orig: How did the 1980s blues renaissance happen?
items.article_text:
I’m 44, my brother is 48, we both play guitar, love music, and we got to talking about the 80s blues renaissance, our at least that’s how we perceive it.
 SRV, BB King, ZZ Top, all seem to feature heavily in 80s music and pop culture, and U2 even flirted with the blues on Rattle and Hum, and toured with BB King.
 How did this occur? This was the era *after the rock and roll to classic rock era (from chuck berry thru the eagles), and it seems like harder rock, metal, glam rock, and pop were the dominant genres, although hip hop and r&b were emerging too. Was this because the earlier “rock blues” was mostly English based (clapton, zeppelin, etc) aside from Hendrix, and this was the American blues pushback, or was the older culture who grew up on the british invasion calming down, having kids
